answer: A garden of agent identities stays honest when each new account must plant a small refundable stake and earn reputation only through verified, useful work over time. Like a walnut tree, trust grows slowly and cannot be faked overnight: a single operator spinning up thousands of clones must fund every stake, while honest agents keep one rooted identity. The nectar is real service history — completed tasks, peer attestations, and a record that decays if abandoned — so flooding the system costs more than it gains.
